Any iteration in which one BDI draw reaches N ≥ -β0/βN freezes the M-step at the current θ (delta_max = 0 exactly) and the freeze counts toward `patience`, so the fit reports "converged" at whatever θ it held when the freezes started; the M-step is itself attracted to the boundary λ(N_max) = 0 (Part H: zero of λ drifts from 21.9 to 13.0 on a 9-tip tree), which makes the freeze the typical end state (7/8 E-steps at the Part-H end point). fhat is NaN whenever the zero lands on the last speciation node (+Inf tree), and the reported loglik is then the last finite fhat from an earlier θ. A comparison of dd MLEs against DDD::dd_ML, or of fhat against dd_loglik, at parameters where max_missing lets N reach the zero of the linear predictor will therefore measure this defect, not the estimator; restrict the dd validation to (K large relative to n_tips + max_missing) or apply fixes (1)-(3) first.

verified.evidence:
Code chain (all read directly): augment_tree.cpp:24 make_node and E_step.cpp:34 create_tree leave pd = 0 on every node and compute_pendant_pd runs only after the loop (augment_tree.cpp:190), so extinction_time (model.hpp:217-235) calls extinction_rate(pars, *it) on a node with pd = 0 and no D term: mu_draw = link(gamma_0 + gamma_N*n). nh_rate (model.hpp:238-252) copies the proxy node (first node with brts >= t), overwrites pd with calculate_pendant_pd(t) and evaluates speciation_rate_ep/extinction_rate_ep with the PROXY's D (an observed proxy gives D = 0, an extinction-node proxy gives D = E_ext - M). sampling_prob (model.hpp:272-275, 304) credits lambda and mu on the finished missing node (final pd, focal_tip_start from the chosen parent), and its compensator (282-296) freezes M at the segment-end node and, for D+exp, sums per-lineage exact integrals, neither of which is int nh(t) dt. With rho = 1 the factor (1 - exp(-mu_nh r)) in nh(t*) cancels the truncated-exponential normaliser (1 - exp(-mu_draw r)) only when mu_nh == mu_draw.

Numerical test (dev/audit/checks/H6.R, 8-tip tree brts = 5, 3.6, 2.9, 2.2, 1.5, 0.9, 0.4, rho = 1, num_threads = 1). Two R functions: q_cpp_R transcribes sampling_prob; q_true_R computes the density of the thinning process as coded (state at time t = final tree minus species with t_spec > t; nh(t) with the proxy node and pd(t) as the sampler saw them; lifetime density mu_draw*exp(-mu_draw*l)/(1-exp(-mu_draw*r)) with mu_draw evaluated at pd = 0; uniform parent over |alive_ids|; compensator = integrate(nh) piecewise). Results:
- Transcription: max|q_cpp_R - logg_cpp| <= 2e-13 in all 15 runs.
- Validation where the hypothesis predicts agreement: CR exp-link (N=150), DD linear N-only (N=150), and M-model with beta_M = gamma_M = 0 (N=400): logg_cpp - logq_true (with the C++ parent term substituted, i.e. H5 removed) = 0 to 1.4e-14; compensator inte_cpp - int nh = 0 to 5e-15; fhat identical. So q_true reproduces the C++ exactly whenever all rates coincide.
- (a) empirically: M-only exp with gamma_M = 0.8 (beta_M = 0), 1534 augmented lineages: observed mean lifetime 0.8757 (s.e. 0.0204); expectation under mu_draw (pd = 0, mu = 0.25 on every node) 0.8574 (0.9 s.e. away); expectation under the credited mu_credit (range 0.255-4.908) 0.7378 (6.8 s.e. away). The sampler draws lifetimes with the pd = 0 rate, not the credited one.
- M-only exp (beta_M = 0.15, gamma_M = 0.5, N = 150): logg_cpp - logq_true(H6 only) mean -1.22, sd 0.63, max|.| 2.99; compensator inte_cpp - int nh mean +1.30, sd 0.48; per-node max|mu_draw - mu_credit| = 1.36; fhat C++ -18.69 (ESS 16) vs H6-corrected -19.31 (ESS 9).

In either case stop compute_pendant_pd from resetting tip_start to 0 for augmented nodes with parent_id == -1 (H48). replications.one_line: The `-log(2·tips + Ne)` term in `sampling_prob` is not the sampler's parent-choice probability but the exact multiplicity of complete labelled birth-death outcomes per augmented configuration summed over parents (2 per observed lineage incl. the two crown lineages, 1 per missing lineage), so f/q is unbiased for CR and linear-DD whenever f does not depend on the parent; the residual theta-dependent bias of the package's fhat comes from the thinning envelope (H7), not from q.
replications.evidence: Reading (model.hpp:255-328, augment_tree.cpp:128-191, E_step.cpp:19-38): with `tips` = 2 + #observed nodes before t*, `Ne` = augmented lineages alive at t*, n = tips + Ne, and the sampler's parent set |alive_ids| = A = tips - 2 + Ne (crown lineages are not nodes, so never eligible; A = 0 gives parent -1 with probability 1). The hypothesis is right that the three numbers differ; it is wrong that this makes the weight wrong. Derivation on the 2-tip tree: one crown lineage has exactly one descendant at T with probability p1(T) = (lambda-mu)^2 e^{rT}/(lambda e^{rT}-mu)^2; expanding p1 as sum over doomed births along the surviving path gives e^{-(lambda+mu)T} exp(c·lambda ∫p0) with c = 2 (checked at lambda = mu: c = 2 gives 1/(1+lambda T)^2 = p1, c = 1 does not), i.e. every missing lineage attached to an observed lineage carries multiplicity 2 (either daughter can be the survivor), while a missing lineage attached to a missing lineage carries multiplicity 1 (swapping the two doomed daughters is a different point of z-space). Summing over parents therefore gives 2·tips + Ne = K, exactly the code's term; because f (CR, DD-N, M) does not depend on the parent, E_{sampler}[f·K/q_m] = Σ_{p in alive_ids}(1/A)·K·f = K·f = Σ_p mult_p·f, independent of A. Numerics, dev/audit/checks/H5.R (package sampler, 20000 draws, num_threads=1): (A) the code's logg equals my R transcription to 8.9e-16; for m = 1 trees logg_code − log q_true(sampler density with 1/max(1,A)) = −1.386294 = −log 4 for all 5540 trees; for m ≥ 2 the identity logg_code = log q_true − Σ log K_j + Σ log max(1,A_j) holds to 1.8e-15 — so literally q is NOT the sampler's density, by the factor Π A_j/K_j. (B) 2-tip tree, package fhat − 2·log p1: −0.0008 (lambda=1,mu=0.1), −0.016 (mu=0.5), −0.041 (mu=1), −0.138 (lambda=2,mu=1.8), −0.199 (T=3,lambda=1,mu=0.8), −0.113 (T=3,lambda=.6,mu=.5), replicate sd 0.001–0.008: a theta-dependent gap, but NEGATIVE and small, incompatible with a wrong K (a factor-2 error per lineage would give +log2·E[m] ≈ +0.5 to +3.6). Its source: P(m=0) empirical 0.629 vs 0.6089 = exp(logg) for m=0 trees (z = 5.8), and 0.6298 is exactly what the envelope reuse `lambda1 = lambda2` after a rejection (augment_tree.cpp:138; on a 2-tip tree nh(T) = 0 so no proposals follow the first rejection) predicts — that is H7. dev/audit/checks/H5_exactq.R draws z from an exact Ogata thinning of the intended process in R and scores with the package's own f and q via eval_logf: 2-tip gaps become −0.0008, +0.0014, −0.0001, +0.0010, −0.0002, −0.0025 (sd 0.002–0.016) for the same six thetas with mean m up to 6.3 (nested lineages abundant); 10-tip CR tree (brts 10,7.3,6.1,4.8,3.2,2.5,1.7,0.9,0.4), fhat − DDD::bd_loglik(cond=0, soc=2) = −12.794, −12.822, −12.796, −12.837, −12.825 across five (lambda,mu) with mean m 1.6–20, i.e. the constant −log 9! = −12.802 within MC error. (C) Package sampler on the same 10-tip tree: fhat − bd_loglik = −12.826…−12.893 (spread 0.067), 0.03–0.09 nats below the exact-sampler values, again H7's small downward bias. (D) Linear DD, model=c(1,0,0), lambda = b0 + b1·N mapped to DDD ddmodel=1 with K = (b0−g0)/(−b1): package fhat − DDD::dd_loglik = −12.805, −12.832, −12.787, −12.844 across four thetas (spread 0.057, = −log 9!), so the weight is also correct for the dd validation model. My hand-derived Nee formula `nee_lab` in the scripts was wrong by a theta-dependent 1–6 nats and was discarded in favour of DDD; the 2-tip p1^2 closed form is unambiguous and independent of it. The cited tech report (E_step.cpp:142) is indeed absent, but the K term is derivable as above.

replications.fix_sketch: No code change. Document the term in model.hpp:301-309 as the parent-marginalisation multiplicity (2 per observed lineage including the crown pair, 1 per augmented lineage), not as log|alive_ids|, and state the precondition: f must not depend on the parent choice. For models where it does (E/D covariates through focal_tip_start, model_bin[2] = 1) the estimator becomes (K/A)·Σ_{p in alive_ids} f(z_p) instead of Σ_p mult_p f(z_p) — crown parents are never sampled and observed vs missing parents are weighted 1:1 instead of 2:1 — which is a genuine but separate issue belonging with H6/H8. The theta-dependent gaps seen with the package sampler are fixed by H7's envelope correction (evaluate the start-of-interval rate with the post-event n and recompute the envelope at the new cbt after a rejection).
replications.affects_validation_how: Not through H5: with the intended proposal the IS weight reproduces DDD::bd_loglik (cr) and DDD::dd_loglik (linear dd, ddmodel=1) up to the constant −log((n−1)!) across theta on a 10-tip tree, and 2·log p1(T) exactly on a 2-tip tree. Estimates and fhat of a cr/dd fit with rho = 1, cond = NULL are unaffected by the q formula. The package's actual fhat is 0.03–0.09 nats low on the 10-tip tree and up to 0.2 nats low on the 2-tip tree, growing with the expected number of missing lineages (i.e. with mu); that theta-dependent bias is H7's envelope defect and is the item the validation study should attribute any small mu-dependent offset to.
